fields.Name: rasa
fields.Description: rasa.io newsletter and audience-engagement platform (v2 API). Syncs contacts, lists, newsletters, blasts, sequences and segments, plus newsletter/blast/sequence engagement events (opens, clicks, deliveries).

Configuration.AuthFlowNote: v2 only (3.0.0; rasa.io directs integrations to v2, and the customer generates the client ID + secret in the rasa.io dashboard, replacing the legacy-dashboard v1 API key). POST /v2/tokens with a JSON body { grant_type: 'client_credentials', client_id, client_secret } (definitions.TokenCreateBody) returns { access_token, token_type: 'Bearer', expires_in } (definitions.ApiResponseTokenCreated). The connector caches the token until 60 s before expires_in and re-mints once on a 401. Super-user clients (account_guid / X-Account-GUID) are not used. The v1 username/password/API-key exchange (POST /v1/tokens) is no longer implemented.
Configuration.AuthHeaderPatternNote: The v2 spec's securityDefinitions.RasaToken names a custom 'rasa-token' header, but the live API rejects it: GET /v2/lists answers 401 with rasa-token alone and 200 with Authorization: Bearer (verified 2026-10-20 on api-dev.rasa.io).

v2.note: account_guid / X-Account-GUID super-user scoping is a rasa.io v2-specific multi-account mechanic, not a general OAuth2 feature.

PaginationDefaults.typeNote: skip/limit query params; the ResponseMetadata envelope carries next_link plus record_count/total_query_count, and the connector follows next_link when present.

v2.evidence: limit parameter descriptions in rasa-v2 swagger.json

perObject.Newsletter/Blast/Sequence Action: created_since (watermark field 'created'). The vendor defaults created_since to seven days ago and rejects a value more than 24 months ago, so the connector sends now − Configuration.maxLookbackDays (725) on a first sync and clamps an older stored watermark up to it.
perObject.Deleted Contact / Newsletter Deleted Con: archived_since (watermark field 'archived_date'). Deleted Contact is fetched once per List (list_id is required).

Configuration.APIVersioningStrategyNote: Version is a URL path segment (basePath /v2 on host api.rasa.io). 3.0.0 targets v2 only; the v1 generation (basePath /v1) is not used — rasa.io: 'we should look into using V2 only. And if anything is missing in the V2 API, we can get it added ASAP.'

universalPK.note: Top-level v2 resources key on 'id' (Contact/Newsletter: string GUID; Blast/Sequence/List: integer). Parent-scoped children are keyed on the parent id plus their own fields (e.g. Newsletter Action: newsletter_id+id+action_type+timestamp+url).

Configuration.WebhooksAvailableNote: No 'webhook' term (case-insensitive) appears anywhere in either rasa-v1-openapi.json or rasa-v2-openapi.json (confirmed via grep -io 'webhook' against both raw spec files -- zero matches), and neither spec documents any push/callback-registration path or tag. Absence is evidenced by exhaustive search of the only two machine-readable sources, not assumed.
Configuration.BulkOperationsAvailableNote: v2 documents POST /contacts/bulk ('Create contacts in bulk', tag: contacts) in rasa-v2-openapi.json. No equivalent bulk-write endpoint exists in the v1 spec (v1 POST /persons is 'adds persons' -- singular add per the OAS summary; PUT /persons is 'update persons' but was not confirmed to accept an array body in this pass, see gaps). BulkOperationsAvailable therefore reflects v2's /contacts/bulk specifically.

Contact.delete: DELETE /contacts/{id} (operationId: archiveContact, summary: 'Archive a contact' -- explicitly a soft-delete/archive, not a hard delete)

v2.note: Confirmed via direct enumeration of every path.<method> in {post,put,patch,delete} across all v2 paths (rasa-v2-openapi.json). Newsletter, Blast, Sequence, and Sequence Message are GET-only in the v2 spec -- no POST/PUT/DELETE documented for any of them (SOURCE_STUDY.md Gaps: 'v2's messaging surface appears read-only by design').

Configuration.ConcurrencyControlNote: Not provable from either spec: no ETag / If-Match / If-Unmodified-Since header, no version/revision field, and no optimistic-lock response code (409/412) is documented on any write operation in rasa-v1-openapi.json or rasa-v2-openapi.json. Left UNSET per the provable-only rule rather than defaulted to 'none' as a guess -- 'none' is itself a claim (the vendor definitively lacks the capability) this pass cannot make from docs alone; a live credentialed conflict-write probe would be needed to confirm no 409/412 exists in practice.

Contact.evidence: DELETE /contacts/{id} operationId: archiveContact, summary: 'Archive a contact', description: 'Archives the contact. The contact's list memberships are not affected.' (rasa-v2-openapi.json). GET /contacts/deleted exists as the v2 tombstone-reconciliation feed (per SOURCE_STUDY.md TaxonomyLeaves #22 'Deleted/Removed Contact').

DeleteSemantics.note: v2 removal is soft (archive). GET /contacts/deleted and /messaging/newsletter/{id}/contacts/deleted are the tombstone feeds.

Configuration.DefaultSyncDirectionNote: Per standing discipline, every object defaults to Pull (read-only) regardless of documented write capability. Bidirectional is opt-in and is NOT recommended as a default for any rasa.io object in this pass -- see METADATA_REPORT preconditions.
Configuration.DefaultConflictResolutionNote: Left UNSET. No ConcurrencyControl signal (ETag/version) is documented (see ConcurrencyControlNote), so 'MostRecent' cannot be justified per the framework rule ('no ETag/version ⇒ don't recommend MostRecent'). Should bidirectional ever be enabled, a snapshot-3-way or SourceWins/DestWins policy chosen per-object at that time is the safer default than guessing here.

OutOfScopeObjectFamilies.reason: Retired in 3.0.0 at the vendor's direction (v2 only). v1 features with no v2 equivalent yet: person sends (vendor: delivery data lives in the v2 action feeds as action_type 'delivered'), person attributes, posts, sections, content pool, lead posts.

Removed in 3.0.1: the list endpoint requires contact_id (HTTP 400 'contact_id query parameter is required'), so a bulk sync would make one request per contact. Subscription create/update writes go with it.
Removed in 3.0.1: internal rasa.io endpoint, not for integrations.
Deferred: windowed roll-ups derivable from the action events.
OutOfScopeObjectFamilies.evidence: /analytics/{newsletter,sequence,blast}/{id}/{activities,articles,images,topics}: date_range enum tops out at last_three_months

OutOfScopeObjectFamilies.reason: On-demand single-contact lookups per the vendor; the bulk connector uses the per-newsletter/blast/sequence feeds instead.
INFORMATIONAL — transport concern (next_link cursor + record_count/total_query_count) that governs the paging loop, not an entity.
INFORMATIONAL — they describe the writable field subset of leaves already in scope (Person, Post, Lead Post, Contact, List), not new resources.
OutOfScopeObjectFamilies.evidence: *CreateBody / *BodyForPost / *BodyForPut / *UpdateBody definitions, all reached only via parameters[].in == 'body' on write operations in both specs.

Configuration.ScopeReason: v2-only catalog (3.0.0): 15 v2 objects carried from 2.x plus 8 new v2 objects — Newsletter/Blast/Sequence Action (insights event feeds, the vendor-recommended bulk engagement source), Newsletter/Blast/Sequence Contact, Newsletter Deleted Contact, Segment. The 18 v1 objects (Person and its children, Post, Lead Post, Content Pool Item, Community, Section, Insight Action/Topic/Topic Score, Analytics Activity/Article/Image/Topic) are retired; see MIGRATION-v3.md. The v2 analytics aggregates (/analytics/{newsletter,sequence,blast}/{id}/…) are deferred: they are windowed roll-ups (date_range up to last_three_months) derivable from the action events. Removed in 3.0.1: Subscription (GET /v2/subscriptions requires contact_id, so a sync would make one call per contact) and Integration Run (an internal rasa.io endpoint, per the vendor).
Configuration.DiscoveryIsAuthoritativeNote: Default false per the brand study — neither v1 nor v2 documents a complete-enumeration/schema-discovery endpoint (e.g. no GET /schema, no GET /objects listing all resource types), so nothing observed as absent during a live sync can be treated as proof of non-existence, and no previously-declared object/field may ever be silently deactivated on the strength of a sync run alone.
Configuration.APIBaseURLNote: Every IO's APIPath carries its own /v2 segment, so the connector composes host root + APIPath (a version-scoped base would double-prefix to /v2/v2/…).

fields.Name: Deleted Contact
fields.Description: Tombstone counterpart to GET /contacts?list_id=<id>. Returns contacts that have left the list — either dropped from it (ContactList.is_archived) or archived globally (Contact.is_archived) — so a sync consumer can reconcile removals incrementally via archived_since instead of diffing a full snapshot. is_archived distinguishes the two modes (gone globally vs only off this list). NOTE: archived_date is a proxy (Contact.updated / ContactList.updated — the row's last-modified time, which for an archival is the archival time) until a dedicated archived_at column exists, mirroring the v1 /persons/deleted feed. (rasa.io v2 — /v2/contacts/deleted, called once per List: list_id is required).

Configuration.doorCorrection: Door corrected from /v2/messaging/sequence/{id}/message/{messageId} (a SINGLE-RECORD detail endpoint — two template vars, the second being this object's own PK) to the nested projection of Sequence.messages off /v2/messaging/sequence. rasa-v2-openapi.json exposes NO /message collection endpoint, so the detail door could never enumerate; definitions.Sequence.messages is an array of SequenceMessage. This is exactly how its three sibling arrays (lists / exclude_lists / subscription_types) are already declared as Sequence List / Sequence Exclude List / Sequence Subscription Type. Docs-derived, consistent with the connector's own established pattern.

Configuration.buildNote: v2 bulk engagement feed (rasa.io: use the per-newsletter/blast/sequence feeds for bulk). The published InsightsAction schema has no contact field, but since rasa.io's 2026-10-20 update each event carries contact_id (resolves via GET /v2/contacts/{id}) and email; 'id' is per event, not the contact.
